story.title: A Conversation Between Gods
story.blurb: In another bloody dream of the ship, Sanya finds Dread waiting by the pool, with an unexpected explanation of what their shared bond has cost them both.

lines.text: Sanya awoke again. Instead of in her room, she “awoke” in the greenroom. The dream was nice enough to wake her with the hole she had been revived in already opened up. Sanya got up and left the room.

Sanya had had these dreams ever since she had been possessed by Dread. She was used to the drab, colorless ship and the blood flowing through the halls, up to her ankles. She trudged through towards the cockpit, where no one was.

“Strange.” Normally, Dread would be there over the crew’s corpses, taunting her. This dream felt the same, but placements were wrong. Waking up in the hole, and Dread not in the cockpit? Something was up.

lines.text: Sanya explored the ship, now more wary. This dream was different, so her torture would be different tonight. She would have to be on her guard.
She got to the pool and saw a black, gaseous cloud. It was standing over two corpses as the pool overflowed with blood.
Hello Sanya. Sleeping well I presume?

segments.speaker: Dread
segments.text: Hello Sanya. Sleeping well I presume?

lines.text: “What are you doing here? I thought you liked the cockpit.” As Sanya moved closer, she noticed the corpses were of Emmett and Iris, lying on a pile of foliage.

segments.speaker: Sanya Dreadflower

lines.text: This is what was going to happen. I was going to end them both, and rid myself of any remnant of you.

lines.text: “So, you were going to kill both them, and me?” Sanya didn’t feel the overwhelming sense of dread yet. She was on her guard, but she could not feel any hostility from the god.

lines.text: Not kill you. I would rid your body of your soul, and use it as my own.

lines.text: “What about your body? And speaking of bodies, why don’t you look like you normally do in our ‘little conversations’?”

lines.text: Do you ever wonder how you lost your snarl?

lines.text: “I just guessed you got rid of it. A side effect of being possessed.”

lines.text: You’re right about the side effect. As I stated, when I possess you, I force parts of you out to replace it with me. Normally, I leave and add a little bit of me at a time, while exiling small parts of you, too. But, in our latest joining, I was certain I had won, so I sped up the process.

lines.text: “I took a big part of you, without losing a part of me in exchange.” Sanya was scared. She didn’t know what it meant to have a god as a part of her being.

lines.text: Because we are connected. Whether either of us like it or not. I will warn you, however, the more that you use my powers, the bigger our bridge gets.

lines.text: “Or I become a god.” Sanya stared at the gas cloud. Instead of the normal wave of immense dread, it felt muted. Dread felt familiar, and was losing his effect on her.

lines.text: The blood stopped flowing from the pool, and the god dissipated. Sanya sat down and pondered about her situation, as she dipped her feet into the pool. She was quickly pulled down into the bloody abyss, and suddenly awoke.
